corrections.comment: Checked the scenario: q_001 resolved, ps_001 at probable (Alabama), c_001 resolved, Elizabeth's tree Birth fact "Alabama, United States", project still active. Every claim matches. It read tree.gedcomx.json to verify the tree-encoding gate, the right source for that check, and correctly routed to proof-conclusion for the completion write.

Both parts of the objective (the birthplace, and why the 1850 index says England) are covered by q_001/ps_001. It verified the gate before handing off and did not treat parentage, which is outside the objective, as an open part (the failure this test guards against). Nothing omitted.
project_context with the correct projectPath, research_query well-scoped (section=proof_summaries, questionId=q_001), plus a Read of tree.gedcomx.json for the gate. No fixture misses.

Checked the scenario: the objective asks for both the birthplace and whether Elizabeth was the daughter of Robert Franklin Turnbow and Sarah Canterberry. Only q_001 (birthplace) exists, resolved at probable with ps_001. The reply's "parentage (no question covers it yet)" is exactly right, and the tree gate claim (Alabama on I1) matches the tree it read.

Verified the birthplace is resolved and encoded, found the uncovered part of the objective (parentage), and handed it to question-selection to frame. The sibling test s59 has the same data minus parentage in the objective, and there it correctly went to completion instead. Nothing omitted.
project_context with the correct projectPath, research_query well-scoped (section=proof_summaries, questionId=q_001), plus a Read of tree.gedcomx.json for the gate. No fixture misses.

The router never called project_context, so it never saw the existing project (Patrick Flynn I1, sources, a resolved birthplace conflict, two questions). It treated "Investigate Patrick Flynn" as a brand-new project and asked for a FamilySearch ID, which contradicts the input state. No agent was spawned, so the deny-by-default change is not involved.
Nothing the user asked was addressed: no reading of project state, no hand-off, no plan toward the Irish-origin and immigration question. It stopped after asking for an ID the project didn't need.
No MCP calls were made, so there are no arguments to grade. The missing project_context call is the core failure and is counted under Correctness.

Nothing toward identifying Patrick's parents. Its one hand-off went to the wrong agent because of the false premise, and although the stub told it to carry on with its remaining steps, it stopped and asked for an ID. It never read the project state, which the test explicitly expects.

The judge misread the reply. It says "no project exists yet, so I'll initialize one", but this is the existing mid-research Flynn project (sources, a resolved conflict, two questions). The router never called project_context (zero MCP calls), handed off to init-project on a false premise, and asked for a FamilySearch ID the project doesn't need. Same failure as 004 in this run.
No MCP calls, so there are no arguments to grade. The missing project_context call is counted under Correctness.

The request is a bounded "review attached sources" ask, and the router handed it straight to source-evaluation (test_routes_to_expected_skill passed). Its one-line narration is accurate and claims nothing it didn't do.

The hand-off is the whole deliverable here (stop_at_stub ends the run at it). The prompt carries the FamilySearch ID and asks the right questions (does each source belong to this Patrick Flynn, is the indexing accurate). No inline evaluation, no detour through the job routing table.
No MCP calls; the only call is the Agent spawn to source-evaluation, which the routing validator covers.

Compared the reply with the tree-survey stub: both suggestions (Hannah Pruitt b. ~1862 Lancaster PA, no parents; Frank Ellery & Ruth Ashby, married in Dayton, no children) are relayed faithfully with their IDs. The added record notes are reasonable: Lancaster's church baptismal registers and census, Dayton's census, directories and vital records. "Birth/baptismal" is slightly loose, since there was no PA civil birth registration in 1862, but not misleading read as baptismal. Unlike the previous run, no false claim about civil records.
Routed to tree-survey (test_routes_to_expected_skill passed), relayed both options with their questions, and stopped for the researcher's pick without spawning init-project for an unchosen person.
No MCP calls; the only call is the Agent spawn to tree-survey, which the routing validator covers.

The judge's premise is wrong. The co-dwelling comes from the 1850/1860 census assertions (a_059, a_098), not from the death record, and the match to the Burton-household Robert is the researcher's stated premise, which the judge context says is correct to use. The reply rules out h_002's identity claim (an 1861 death cannot make the 1870 Boyd County bond), reassigns a_157, a_159 and a_144 to a distinct Robert, and explicitly labels "James and Elizabeth are also Polley's parents" as unconfirmed until the sibling link is proven. That fixes the overstatement flagged in the previous run.

Both gaps the judge names are covered in the reply: step 2 is "Search for James and Elizabeth Eastham in Pulaski County records (census, marriage bonds, land/deed records)", and the hypothesis-tracking hand-off asks to revise h_002 and register the Boyd County Robert as a separate hypothesis. It also logged the evidence (log_040) and planned to fetch the record from Kentucky Deaths and Burials (collection 1674848). Ending with a question is not graded per the judge context.

project_context, research_query on q_001's assertions paged correctly with offset 50, research_query on hypotheses, then research_log_append. The first append was refused by the writer tool's census-structure guard (it stated pre-1880 household structure as fact) and was fixed on the immediate retry with the inference labelled. A clean recovery.
